title: Evaluating Accuracy and Probabilistic Reliability of Zero-Shot Time Series Foundation Models

primary_sources.paraphrase: arXiv abstract (v1, 22 Sep 2026, accepted at ADBIS 2026): six zero-shot foundation models on energy, traffic and finance data against statistical baselines and one supervised model. They win on accuracy but trade accuracy against calibration; xLSTM-based models calibrate most robustly, patch transformers lose calibration at long horizons.

Full text: Chronos-2, TiRex, Moirai-2.0, Sundial, Toto, TimesFM at defaults, all univariate, against ARIMA, running average, drift and a small PatchTST. Polish national hourly load (17 months, 2024-25), horizons 12 to 672 h without 168; sMAPE and 80% interval coverage error; no intervals, window count not given. TiRex is named the most consistent calibrator.

Authors' repository, Apache-2.0, 21 commits, no releases: a parquet file of the benchmark forecasts and a notebook that rebuilds the plots and aggregations. No model ids or revisions and no hardware note; the code that produced the forecasts was not seen in the file list.

TiRex model repository (central model): created 2025-05-26; the weights file model.ckpt was last changed in that first commit (d76a39c). An ONNX export was added 2026-02-05 and the head commit of 2026-11-13 only edits the model card. Licence tag: nx-ai-community-license.

NXAI Community License (May 2025), modelled on the Llama 3 community licence: use, modification and distribution allowed with an attribution notice; a group with more than EUR 100 million annual revenue needs a separate commercial licence to put the model in a commercial product.

claims.text: Across the three data types the xLSTM-based TiRex gives the most consistent interval calibration; on Polish national load its 80% interval coverage error stays between 0.01 and 0.04 across the tested horizons and contexts.
claims.metric: ICE of the 80% interval (upper end of the reported 0.01-0.04 range)
claims.baseline: the other five foundation models and PatchTST

claims.text: On Polish national load at a 12 h horizon Chronos-2, TiRex and Sundial reach sMAPE of 3.92 to 3.95% against about 14% for ARIMA.
claims.metric: sMAPE (%), upper end of the 3.92-3.95 range

claims.text: On Polish national load at a 672 h horizon Chronos-2 has sMAPE 6.4% (Moirai-2.0 6.6%) against 19% for ARIMA.

At a 24 h horizon on Polish load, Chronos-2 improves with longer context: sMAPE falls from 6.70% to 4.4% and interval coverage error from 0.17 to 0.04 between the shortest and longest contexts reported.
claims.horizon: 24 h, context 120 h to about 600 h
claims.baseline: the same model at context 120 h (6.70%)

claims.text: On 1-second traffic counts at an 1800-step horizon, TimesFM's interval coverage error reaches 0.73 (Moirai-2.0 0.56) while Chronos-2 and TiRex stay under 0.06.
On daily S&P 500 ETF closes at a 252-day horizon TiRex has sMAPE 8.34% (Chronos-2 8.64%) against 9.68% for ARIMA.

relevance.rationale: One of three datasets is hourly electric load (Polish national aggregate, not PJM zonal); the other two are 1-second traffic counts and daily ETF prices (3 on the load part). Load horizons are 12, 24, 72, 144, 288, 576 and 672 h: day-ahead is tested and the grid brackets a week, but 168 h itself is not run and numbers are given only for 12, 24 and 672 h (2). Every model is run on the series alone; no weather or other covariate is used (1).

checks.notes: Central model: TiRex, the model the headline calibration claim singles out (xLSTM-based, most consistent calibrator). Chronos-2 carries most of the load numbers and is called the most balanced; it is the secondary model. Training overlap (our run): TiRex's weights file model.ckpt was committed 2025-05-26 and not changed since, before the first scored week (2025-11-10), so all 52 scored weeks follow it: low. The paper does not say which revision it loaded. Pre-registration: none mentioned in the full text. Replication: one search found only the arXiv record and unrelated studies; unknown. Evidence strength moderate: the forecasts and an aggregation notebook are public under Apache-2.0 and the headline claim is descriptive, but there are no intervals, seeds or repeats, the number and dates of test windows are not given (test_window_days is null for the load and SPY claims; the traffic set spans 2 hours, so 0), and the paper does not say how ARIMA's inputs or orders were set. The foundation models all received the same univariate series. ACCEPT_RUN for a study: the accuracy half of the headline (a zero-shot model against a simple baseline on hourly load) can be re-measured with TiRex on load history only; the calibration half cannot be read from our leaderboard's point metrics. Unverified: all numbers were read by a summarising fetch of the HTML and not checked against the PDF or the parquet file; values for H=72 to 576 and for Toto, TimesFM and the drift baseline on load were not found; the text cites a context of 624 h that is outside the stated grid (max 600); the repository's last commit date and whether it contains the forecasting pipeline; whether the repository README (slightly different title) describes the same version of the study. models_ff/run_ff.py has no TiRex entry and models/pins.json was not checked for one, so the FoundationForecast TiRex wrapper is untested in our environment. The paper ran on a T4 GPU; CPU runtime for TiRex within the 60 minute limit is not verified. The NXAI licence was read through a summarising fetch.

license: NXAI Community License (attribution required; commercial licence needed above EUR 100 million annual revenue)
label: ACCEPT_RUN
label_reason: The paper has a primary source with public forecasts, includes hourly national electric load, and its central model TiRex is a FoundationForecast wrapper with weights from May 2025, so a univariate row can be measured on our benchmark now. The evidence is only moderate and the fit is partial: no 168 h horizon, no covariates, no intervals, and the headline calibration finding is not something our point-metric receipt can test.
implementation_hint: TiRex through FoundationForecast, univariate: add a SPECS entry to models_ff/run_ff.py for NX-AI/TiRex (weights file model.ckpt, commit d76a39c of 2025-05-26; pin a revision in models/pins.json) and run it on load history only, labelled univariate. Gate origins first, on CPU. Secondary model already on the leaderboard: amazon/chronos-2 via models/chronos2.py. The receipt can compare point error with the temperature-only regression at 168 h; the paper's own comparison is against ARIMA at 12 and 672 h with sMAPE, and its calibration claim (80% interval coverage, the same 0.1/0.9 quantiles run_ff.py requests) would need a coverage metric the receipt does not carry. Moirai-2.0, Sundial, Toto and TimesFM are the other models tested (ff_univariate).
